correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the proof from the pinned RESULT.md and all seven blobs at Git tree b6d7dd0c95b83ed4642efb23f7ef7524c03b669f. For any absolute normalized N, triangle inequality and coordinate monotonicity give Θ≤max over nonnegative sphere of min{N(1+c,d),N(c,1+d)}. Octahedrality gives almost aligned norming-functional witnesses in each real component, with 0≤c,d≤1 and ||x+cξ||≥(1−ε)(1+c), establishing the reverse supremum uniformly for all X,Y,x,y. For N_t the scalar expression is F=max{1+min(c,d),(1+c+d)/(1+t)}. On the positive sphere, min(c,d)≤(1+t)/2 and c+d≤1+t; both bounds are attained by c=d=(1+t)/2. Thus Θ=max{(3+t)/2,(2+t)/(1+t)} exactly for all 0≤t≤1. The crossing polynomial is t²+2t−1, yielding the sharp unique minimum 1+1/√2 at t=√2−1; endpoint values 2, and strict interior deficit. Independent SymPy algebra and 131199 rational boundary evaluations for 433 parameter samples were replayed from a newly written checker, alongside 433 exact diagonal equalities. The continuous theorem rests on the analytic inequalities, not finite grids.
residual_risks: No formula claimed for arbitrary finite subsets or for average-roughness constants; finite tests do not certify unrestricted spaces.

value.rationale: The two prescribed axis points are precisely the natural finite witness test in the established positive-octahedrality preservation criterion. For a canonical nested deformation connecting the classical preserving ℓ1 and ℓ∞ norms, the result provides an exact quantitative obstruction throughout the nonpreserving interior, a surprising nonmonotone phase switch at a regular-octagon parameter, and a reusable scalar reduction for all absolute norms and all octahedral summands. It is an exact natural invariant, not a random parameter slice or a previously tabulated special case; future work on near-octahedrality in absolute sums can directly reuse the sharp shortfall.
residual_risks: This is one distinguished two-axis finite test, not a complete modulus over all finite subsets or other roughness indices.

final_claim: For all 0≤t≤1 and nonzero real Banach spaces X,Y with octahedral norms, any fixed x∈S_X,y∈S_Y have simultaneous two-axis witness constant Θ_t(x,y)=max{(3+t)/2,(2+t)/(1+t)} in the absolute sum X⊕_{N_t}Y, N_t(a,b)=max{|a|,|b|,(|a|+|b|)/(1+t)}; the unique largest shortfall from 2 occurs at t=√2−1, where Θ_t=1+1/√2; endpoints Θ=2 and all interior Θ<2.
